name: Inkling-2-Mini-Decision
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini (config.json max_position_embeddings 1048576). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: 20 of 24 layers are sliding-window attention (sliding_window_size 1024), 4 layers are global (local_layer_ids lists the 20 local layers); GQA 24 Q / 8 KV heads at head_dim 128
notes: ADDED 2026-11-23 by the trending sweep. A LoRA post-train of thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini (catalog record `inkling-2-mini`), not a new base: same config.json, same MoE backbone, so architecture/params/kv geometry are inherited from the base record and only the heads are new (LoRA r=32 on attention q/k/v/o/linear ~17.5M params, a 1.2M CoreGateHead halting gate, a 6.0M JointSchemaHead). PARAMS: safetensors.total 25,607,222,784 vs the base's 26,388,646,440, a 781,423,656 delta explained by the card itself - the lm_head and the ~0.43B vision_tower are dropped for text decisioning, which is why 25.6 < 26.4. This is a DECISION model (task=decision): it takes a state plus typed questions (choice/noul/score) and emits per-option probabilities in ONE forward pass with zero reasoning tokens, so chat benchmarks say nothing about it and it is excluded from the worth-running ranking by construction. EVIDENCE, stated honestly: the card does NOT print an Inkling-2-Mini base column on any decision test, and none can exist - the generative base has no decision head, so an absolute base score would require a harness the card never describes. What it does print is (a) self-consistency across loop depth, Loop 1 39.89% -> Loop 3 66.67% on hard-v1/dev (+26.78 pp) and 42.56% -> 66.82% on hard-v1/test, and (b) a same-test cross-model comparator, Kev-9B v1 (9B dense, catalog decision_index dec-kev-9b) at 58.2/58.4 on hard-v1 dev/test against this model's 66.67/66.82 - a +8.4 pp win at 5.4B effective active. The task prompt's 'own column beats the base column' gate is therefore NOT met in the literal sense; the record is justified under the decision-model rule (4c) as a classified contender, with the gap between 'beats a same-size decision model' and 'beats its base' left visible rather than papered over. LOSSES are recorded in benchmarks[]: Kev-27B 86.3 vs 85.56 on decision-v7/test, and Qwen3.5-4B-Hmm 70.9 vs 63.5 on LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions. NOT ON THE DECISION INDEX: the upstream JEV space (multimodalart/jev-decision-index) had not listed it as of 2026-11-23 (lastModified 2026-11-21) and its row in data/decision_index.jsonl was therefore not added - no index, latency or ECE figure is invented here. The card's own GPU numbers are RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, batch-1, threshold 0.90: 81.4 ms median (97.4 mean) to first decision, 1.68x faster than fixed Loop 3 at -0.07 pp accuracy; these are latency, not a benchmark score, and are quoted only here in notes. benchmarks.name: hard-v1 test (untrained OOD decision set)
benchmarks.config: Card table 'Loop 1 vs Loop 2 vs Loop 3', row hard-v1/test (n=1,088): Loop 3 = 66.82%. Same table/model card prints the comparator Kev-9B v1 (9B dense decision model, catalog decision_index dec-kev-9b) at 58.4 on hard-v1/test and 58.2 on hard-v1/dev, so this is a same-test cross-model win of +8.4 pp at 5.4B active vs 9.7B dense. Harness not printed; all rows are the author's own runs on the author's own splits, so hard-v1 is NOT an independent benchmark.

benchmarks.name: hard-v1 dev (untrained OOD decision set)
benchmarks.config: Card table, row hard-v1/dev (n=1,083): Loop 3 = 66.67%, up from 39.89% at Loop 1 (+26.78 pp). Comparator Kev-9B v1 printed on the same card at 58.2 (hard-v1/dev). Author's own split, not an independent benchmark.

benchmarks.name: decision-v7 test (routine decisions)
benchmarks.config: Card table, row decision-v7/test (n=1,440): Loop 3 = 85.56%, +3.27 pp over Loop 1. LOSS recorded: the card prints Kev-27B (27B dense) at 86.3 on the same set, so this model is 0.74 pp behind a 27B while running 5.4B active. Also recorded: re-verified 86.04% (1,239/1,440) after merge_and_unload + causal_conv1d.

benchmarks.name: typed-decisions (LocalLLaMA, test split)
benchmarks.config: Independent run by the author on Modal A100-80GB, 22 Nov 2026, LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions 'all' config test split (400 cases / 2,000 decisions), zero-shot, scored with the benchmark's own code; default threshold 0.90 = 0.635 accuracy, ECE 0.041, Brier 0.179. LOSS recorded: the catalog's Qwen3.5-4B-Hmm scores 70.9 on typed-decisions (2,000 workflow decisions) and Qwen3.5-4B base 59.6, so this model does NOT beat the size class on this test.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro (partial sample, 3,272 of 12,032)
benchmarks.config: Author's own time-boxed run, seeded random 3,272-question sample of TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro test, each question asked as one 'choice' question with lettered options. A sample estimate, explicitly NOT a leaderboard score - do not rank against full-set MMLU-Pro rows.
